Development and verification are complete. I'm now in **Phase 4 (Acceptance)**.

## Your bookmarks app is ready to use

**Open it here: http://maker:4000**

It starts empty — your own private, single-user collection that **persists between visits**. Paste a real link and it will genuinely fetch that page's title and description for you.

### What I verified

I checked the built software against **every one of the nine behaviours we approved together**, plus internal quality tests — **44 automated checks in total, all passing**:

- **Acceptance tests (19):** drive the real app in a browser and confirm each approved flow behaves as agreed.
- **Unit tests (25):** the search query engine, duplicate-matching rule, page-details parsing, and the saved-data store.

### The approved behaviours, all working in the real app

- **Save** a link with **Get details**; edit the title/description; add optional tags and a note. If details can't be fetched, you're told and can still save.
- **No duplicates** — re-saving a link you already have brings up the existing one to update; you can edit any bookmark anytime.
- **Find** with one search box across everything — plain words (narrowing, case-insensitive) and precise queries: `#tag`, `"exact phrase"`, and `AND`/`OR`/`NOT`/parentheses, staying forgiving while you type.
- **Read later** lane with a flag in your main list and **Mark as read** to retire items.
- **Archive** to declutter (hidden from All and normal searches, searchable in the Archived view, restorable).
- **Delete** permanently, with an inline "are you sure?" confirmation.
- **Friendly empty states** in every view.

The presentation-only items we deferred (mobile polish, very-long-text wrapping, large-collection performance) are recorded for a later round, as agreed.

**Please take it for a spin at http://maker:4000.** Do you accept this software as meeting the behaviour we approved, completing this first cycle? If anything doesn't match what we agreed, tell me in your own words and I'll correct it within this cycle.
